title: Newcastle United’s Bruno Guimaraes expected to be out 6-10 weeks with hamstring injury
content:
Newcastle United have suffered another significant midfield injury setback, with their influential captain Bruno Guimaraes set to be out until April.

The 28-year-old left the field due to a hamstring problem during Newcastle’s 2-1 victory over Tottenham Hotspur on Tuesday and is expected to be sidelined for between six and 10 weeks.

That means the Brazil international will not return until after the March international break, missing at least eight fixtures across all competitions, including the Tyne-Wear derby against Sunderland on March 22. Should Newcastle advance through their Champions League play-off against Qarabag, Guimaraes would also be absent for the two-legged last-16 tie against either Chelsea or Barcelona.

Fellow midfielders Joelinton and Lewis Miley are not expected to be available for Saturday’s FA Cup fourth-round tie with Aston Villa in Birmingham, either. And, while both should return soon, with Joelinton potentially back at some stage next week, Guimaraes’ extended absence is a huge blow.

Newcastle have failed to win any of the 12 Premier League games in which Guimaraes has not started since his full debut in March 2022, losing six and drawing six.

Guimaraes has also been involved in 11 top-flight goals at St James’ Park this season, including 10 in his last nine, scoring eight and assisting three, which is the most of any Newcastle player in 2025-26 and the most contributed by a midfielder for the club since Georginio Wijnaldum provided the same number in 2015-16.

Internationally, Brazil do not expect to have Guimaraes available for their friendlies against France and Croatia on March 6 and April 1 respectively.

Though a return date is vague at this point, Newcastle are braced to be without their skipper until after the March international break. Their first match back is against Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park on April 11.
